question.problem:
Which of the following probabilities could be approximated using the normal approximation of the binomial distribution?

I. The probability of a student getting $9$ correct answers on a test with $12$ questions if each question has $3$ options and the student answers all questions randomly.

II. The probability of finding more than $50$ people with blue eyes in a randomly selected sample of $250$ if $40%$ of the population has blue eyes.

III. The probability that a biased coin lands on tails $35$ times out of $50$ coin flips if the probability that a single flip landing on tails is $0.6.$
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Let's now examine each situation.

- In situation I, we have $n=12$ and $p=\frac{1}{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =12\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =4 \\  & ≯5.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, we *cannot* use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation II, we have $n=250$ and $p=0.4.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =250\cdot 0.4 \\  & =100 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =250\cdot (1-0.4) \\  & =150 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation III, we have $n=50$ and $p=0.6.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =50\cdot 0.6 \\  & =30 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =50\cdot (1-0.6) \\  & =20 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
